newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota sunflower harvest advances.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota sunflower harvest advances.

text.p: Clear, dry weather allowed North Dakota producers to make rapid progress on sunflower combining during the week ended Sunday, according to the weekly state crop report.

Harvesting of other late-season crops also continued until week-ending rain and snow halted fieldwork. Harvesting of corn for grain continued to lag the average level because of high moisture content, the report said.
Sunflower harvesting advanced to 58 percent complete, versus 18 during the previous week, 54 last year and the five-year average of 44 percent.
Corn for grain harvested 27 pct vs 10 w/a, 49 y/a, 45 avg.
Flaxseed harvested 96 pct vs 90 w/a, 97 y/a, 95 avg.
Sorghum mature 97 pct vs 94 w/a, 97 y/a, 93 avg.
Potatoes dug 98 pct vs 88 w/a, 94 y/a, 98 avg.
Soybeans harvested 92 pct vs 76 w/a, 69 y/a, 85 avg.
Sugarbeets lifted 97 vs 88 w/a, 71 y/a, 89 avg.
Pasture and range condition was rated 26 pct good to excellent, versus 38 percent at that level last week.
